title: Design a live leaderboard
dek: During an IPL match, Zotato runs a quiz: a question after every few overs, 20 seconds to answer, points for being right. 50 lakh people play, and each wants the top 100 and their own rank, updated seconds after every question.

items: A sorted set (in Redis) keeps players ordered by score: adding points, reading the top 100 and finding one player's rank are each fast, even with lakhs of players.
The hard moment is the 20-second window: up to 50 lakh answers arrive at once. Save the answers first, and add the points when the question closes, in batches.
One sorted set can't take 50 lakh updates in seconds, so split players across a few shards. The top 100 is the best of each shard's top 100, merged.
A player's exact rank across shards means asking every shard. Keeping counts per score band gives a close rank ("about 80,000th, top 2%") with one lookup.
The saved answers are the truth. The leaderboard is a fast copy that can always be rebuilt from them.
Players answer each question within 20 seconds; right answers score points, faster answers score a little more.
Show the top 100 and each player's own rank and score, updated within a few seconds of each question closing.
Ties are broken by who reached the score first.
Out of scope here: friends' leaderboards (a follow-up), prizes, and cheating detection beyond the basics.

body.label: Qualities to aim for
head: Quality
Target
rows: Ranks updated within 5 seconds of a question closing
Every right answer counted once; ranks can be approximate, scores can't
Top 100 and my rank in under 100 ms
50 lakh players, 40 questions a match, all answering in the same 20 seconds

items: Answers: 50 lakh in 20 seconds is 2.5 lakh writes a second for those 20 seconds, then almost nothing until the next question.
Score updates: if 60% answer correctly, that's 30 lakh point updates per question. Done in 5 seconds, 6 lakh updates a second.
Plan on about 1 lakh updates a second per shard (pipelined, Redis can do several times that), so 6 to 8 shards finish a question's updates in about 5 seconds.
Reads: after each question, most players open the leaderboard: 50 lakh reads in a minute is about 80,000 a second. The top 100 is the same for everyone, so cache it.
Memory: 50 lakh players × about 100 bytes in a sorted set is around 500 MB in total; small for Redis.
Answer: `match_id`, `question_id`, `player_id`, `choice`, `received_at`. One per player per question (a unique key).
Score: per player and match, `points` and `reached_at` (when they got to those points), in the sorted sets.
Band counts: per match, how many players are in each score band, updated with the scores.

body.label: API
body.say: Send an answer (one per question; a resend changes nothing). Read the top 100. Read your own score and rank.

body.cap: Answers are saved as they arrive. When the question closes, the scorer adds points in batches to sorted sets split across Redis shards. The API serves the top 100, cached for a second, and each player's own rank.

body.x: Answering and scoring are separated by time: the 20-second window only saves answers, which is a simple append. Scoring happens once, after the window, when the right answer is known.

body.name: First try
body.kind: SORT THE TABLE ON EVERY READ
body.what: Keep scores in a database table and run ORDER BY points DESC LIMIT 100, and COUNT(*) WHERE points > mine for a rank.
body.use: Correct and simple for a few thousand players.
body.avoid: With 50 lakh rows and 80,000 reads a second, each rank query counts lakhs of rows. The database melts right after every question.
body.ex: At the end of the 12th over, every player opens the leaderboard and the page takes 20 seconds.
body.like: Re-sorting the whole class register every time a student asks their position.

body.name: Better
body.what: Keep scores in Redis sorted sets, players split across shards by a hash of their id. Add points with one command per player, in batches. Top 100: take each shard's top 100 and merge. My rank: add up, over the shards, how many players have more points than me.
body.use: Each operation is fast, and the shards share the burst of updates.
body.avoid: An exact rank asks every shard on every request. Fine for 8 shards; for more, use band counts (below).
body.ex: After the 12th over, 30 lakh scores are updated across 8 shards in about 5 seconds, and the top 100 is cached for everyone.
body.like: Eight house captains each keep their house's list in order; the school's top 10 is the best of their lists.

body.cap: Keep how many players have each band of scores. Ananya has 340: everyone in the higher bands is ahead of her, and an estimate of where 340 sits inside her band finishes the job (or keep a count for every score: there are only about 1,000). One small lookup gives a close rank and her top percentage.

items: Update the band counts in the same batch as the scores: the scorer adds up each batch's band moves and applies them as one update per band.
For anyone outside the top few thousand, show the band-based rank and a percentage. Nobody can tell 80,412 from 80,399, and "top 2%" means more to them.
For the top few thousand, use exact ranks from the shards; that's where people care about each place.

Ties: whoever reached the score first ranks higher. Pack both into the sorted set's score: points first, then a part that's bigger for earlier times (milliseconds since the match started, so it fits). The scorer sets the whole score with ZADD rather than adding to it.
One answer per player per question: a unique key on the answers table. A resend from a bad network changes nothing.
Answers after the 20 seconds are refused by the server's clock, not the phone's.
If a shard is lost, rebuild it from the saved answers. Scores are never kept only in Redis.
Junior / mid: a sorted set for scores, top-N and rank commands, a cache for the top 100.
Senior: the 20-second burst and saving answers before scoring, sharding the sets, merging top lists, tie-breaking.
Lead: band counts for cheap ranks, rebuilding from answers, server-side deadlines, read caching after each question.
"Friends' leaderboard?" Fetch the scores of your 50 friends by id from the shards and sort them; it's a small list.
"Weekly leaderboard across matches?" A separate sorted set per week, added to after each match; start a new one each Monday.
"Someone answers with a script in 50 ms?" Faster answers earn only a little more, cap the speed bonus, and flag answers faster than a human can read.
"Show live score changes as they happen?" Push the top 10 and the player's own new rank over an open connection after each question, not every update.
"How do you test it?" Simulate 50 lakh answers in 20 seconds against a test copy and check the ranks match a full sort of the saved answers.

body.x: A leaderboard during a match is a spike at moments you know in advance. The IND vs PAK challenge is the same night, for video.
body.go: Try the IND vs PAK challenge

practice.brief: Each test sends answers and leaderboard reads. Each request is one query against the sorted sets, which a cache keeps (90% of reads); 40% of queries are score updates. Scoring can follow a moment after the answer. Your Clients' own rate is ignored. The tests send a slice of the quiz traffic (up to 70,000 answers and reads a second, against the full 2.5 lakh), so the Lab's numbers stay small; at full size it is the same design with more shards.

tests.desc: 10,000 requests a second: players checking their rank.

tests.desc: At 8 pm the big quiz round starts: 70,000 answers and reads a second for 15 minutes.

tests.name: A server group dies
tests.desc: At the peak (40,000 a second) the busiest group of servers crashes; it is back 5 minutes later.

checks.label: At least 99.5% of requests still succeed
No server group that every request depends on (no single point of failure)

tests.name: The database fails
tests.desc: At the peak the busiest database crashes. With a standby in another zone it fails over in 2 minutes; without one it is down for 30.

checks.label: At least 99.8% of requests still succeed
Every database has a standby in another zone (Multi-AZ)

tests.name: A sensible bill
tests.desc: A whole day at the normal rate (10,000 a second). Paying for far more than the traffic needs fails, like a memory limit.

tests.name: A right answer scores
tests.desc: p1 answers question 12 correctly and earns 50 points. The answer is accepted at once; workers add the points to the board a moment later.

Leaderboard reads a second after a question
Memory for all scores
est.how: 50 lakh × ~100 bytes in a sorted set

decisions.q: The top 100, and my rank among 50 lakh players, in under 100 ms. How?
options: ORDER BY score in the database for each request
A sorted set in memory, ordered by score
A ranking recomputed every minute by a batch job
decisions.why: Sorting 50 lakh rows per request is far too slow, and a ranking from a minute ago misses the question that just closed. A sorted set keeps the order as scores change and answers any rank quickly.

decisions.q: A question closes and 30 lakh right answers score at once. Then?
options: Each answer request updates the sorted set before it returns
Turn away answers that arrive after the first few seconds
Queue the answers; workers add the points at a steady pace
decisions.why: The queue absorbs the burst; ranks are a few seconds behind for a moment, and nothing falls over. Updating inside every request makes the burst hit the sorted sets all at once; dropping late answers is unfair.

decisions.q: The in-memory store restarts. What about the rankings?
options: Rebuilt from the scores kept in the database
Rebuilt from the players' phones, which keep their own score
Started again from zero for the rest of the match
decisions.why: Memory is fast but not the record. The database keeps every score, so the sorted set can be rebuilt; phones can be tampered with, and starting from zero is unfair to everyone.

hints.x: Scores must be exact; ranks can be a little approximate. Which requirement does that relax?
Everything happens in 20-second bursts: answers, then score updates, then everyone reading the leaderboard.
POST an answer (202), GET the top 100, GET my own rank.
Answers don't need scoring inside the request. Queue them; workers update the scores.
Scores live in sorted sets in memory (a Cache in the Lab); the top 100 is the same for everyone, so it's read from the cache.
The burst is 3× the peak: size the API servers for it before 8 pm; two groups everywhere.

wrong.name: One server group
wrong.why: When it crashes, nothing answers for 5 minutes.

wrong.name: Single-zone database
wrong.why: A crash keeps it down for 30 minutes.

wrong.name: No queue
wrong.why: The burst hits the database directly and crashes it.

wrong.name: Biggest everything
wrong.why: Passes the load but costs far more than the traffic needs.

wrong.name: Right sizes, general parts
wrong.why: The sizes and redundancy are right, but no component does the job this problem turns on, so the design would carry the traffic without doing what was asked.

wrong.name: Scores without players
wrong.why: Scores are stored by match, with no row per player to add to.
